doc.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Latin jazz versus jazz Latin and respecting the sources
summary: Discussing Ray Barretto's distinction, he stresses equal parts and learning a style before mixing it, saying many artists do so irresponsibly.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, you know I had a conversation once with Ray Barretto where he talked about the difference between Latin, a true sense of Latin Jazz and what he referred to as Jazz Latin. I asked him for examples, about different bands and whatnot, Tito Puente at the time had a small group. Poncho Sanchez and others, and he referred—respectfully—to what a lot of others people were doing as Jazz Latin. A lot of people were doing Jazz with Latin elements, as opposed to doing what he felt was true Latin Jazz was when you had a more thorough immersion into Latin music, using Jazz elements. What is your sense of that?

Well, I am, I am not a very good philosopher, but what I can say that what Mario means with that is that most of the elements used in the so called Latin Jazz are the elelments of Afro- Cuban music, or Brazilian music. They are totally separated; they have the same roots—
Well, I think that’s what, that’s kind of what he was referring to was true Latin Jazz is when there’s a true meeting of the form—
A true meeting of the form—

Equal parts. Um, I probably was one of the few using elements of the music of Venezuela, for example. Venezuela, Argentina, mainly Brazil, and some of the music of Mexico, a lot of places south of the border.
So Mario was referring to you in that way because you had gone beyond—
Afro-Cuban and you had begun to incorporate more of the music of the Americas and all.

Yea, and I tried to do the best, because many, many Jazz artist—and I also put classical in there—they had been incorporating the elements in a very irresponsible way. Without, in order to mix one thing with another, you have to know the elements of both sides, you know. Pay respect to the music and all.
Which is kind of how Ray was referring to as well.
Probably he was talking about the same thing, yea. In order to want an element to a certain style of music, you have to learn the most that you can from that style of music.
